newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Gamma trade boosts Bund volatility.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Gamma trade boosts Bund volatility.

text.p: January Bund volatility is heading higher on LIFFE, as traders make up for the dearth of volume by indulging in gamma trading, brokers said on Thursday.

Concerns over year-end book squaring, along with the proximity of many traders' and brokers' performance-related yearly bonuses, have resulted in low volume and an unwillingness to put new trades in place.

"The low volume means it's easy to push the market around, which is an ideal situation for gamma trading," said Luke White, a broker at Fimat Futures in London. "Even if the volume is low, you can make gamma rent."

Gamma is the measure of change in the delta of an option, compared with the price change in the underlying future. Delta measures the change in the value of an option's premium compared with the underlying contract.
Going long of gamma involves buying an option, and hedging the position in the futures market. As the underlying Bund contract oscillates the position is regularly readjusted.
"If you do that enough times, you can do quite well," said White, adding that the low pre-Christmas volumes made this an easier strategy to achieve.
Implied volatility of January options on March Bund futures was at 7.3 percent by 1300 GMT, up from 6.4 percent at midday on Wednesday, and up from 7.00 percent at Wednesday's close.

Brokers said the spread of volatility between January and later-dated options had widened, where gamma trading is less prevalent. February options vol rose to 5.9 percent from 5.25 on Wednesday, while March vol was unchanged at 6.0 percent.
March Bund futures were up 0.12 at 100.08 by 1300 GMT.
Volatility was broadly higher across the board, as there was still general nervousness the bond market could be heading for another leg down, traders said.

Activity in January and February options was clustered around the 100.00, 100.50 and 101.00 strikes, with both puts and calls sharing the volume. In the over-the-counter options market, brokers said volatility was shadowing activity on the futures.
"It's quite lacklustre out there," said an OTC broker in London. "The three-month Bund (price) volatility is hovering around 6.0 percent."
Activity in the OTC market was limited to position closing, he said.
